clue.text: Pack round with tar

parts.note: a pack of playing cards is a deck
a round of applause is also called a hand, as in 'give them a big hand'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wrap a package with tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' and 'round' look like verbs for wrapping something up; both are nouns. TAR is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is slang for a sailor, and a sailor working on the ship's deck is one kind of seaman.

clue.text: Starfish?

parts.note: split as star plus fish: a southern constellation that also names a gamefish

explanation.definitionFit: Dorado is both a southern-sky constellation and a golden tropical fish, so a star group and a fish.

clue.text: Taxi hired to go round Brazilian city with the top down

indicators.note: to go round means the first pieces surround the city

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
let means rented out or hired
Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A hired taxi drives round Rio with its roof down.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a convertible car whose roof folds back, so it can be driven roofless.

clue.text: Furtive denigration can have this effect

explanation.surface: Sly slander can produce a certain result.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to the proverb 'give a dog a bad name and hang him': speaking ill of a dog can get it hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangdog means shamefaced and sneaking, and the proverb says a bad name gets a dog strung up.

clue.text: Bereaved mother gets Ulster award

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
an OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A grieving mother receives an honour in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Niobe's children were all killed by Apollo and Artemis, and she wept until turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this queen lost all her children and became the image of a grieving parent.

clue.text: Remove the cad in disorder

indicators.note: being in disorder means the six letters of these two words are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to get rid of a badly behaved man who is in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach something is to separate it and take it off, a synonym of removing it.

clue.text: How one might be heard to address one's dearest.

definitions.text: How one might be heard to address one's dearest.

parts.words: How one might be heard to address one's dearest.
parts.note: spoken, an endearment for a loved one; and a phrase meaning one's most cherished possession

explanation.definitionFit: Said out loud it sounds like an affectionate 'you lamb', and from Nathan's parable it means one's most treasured possession.

clue.text: A portion said to be returned by religious leader in nurse's absence

indicators.note: to be returned means the remaining letters are read backwards
the nurse's absence means her letters are taken out

parts.note: an ayatollah is a Shiite religious leader
an ayah is a nursemaid in India

explanation.surface: A share, it is said, will be handed back by a cleric once the nurse is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A ... said' hints that the answer sounds like 'a lot'. Removing AYAH from AYATOLLAH leaves TOLLA, and 'to be returned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To portion something out is to share it out, a synonym for allotting.

clue.text: Rhetorical question in: an embarrassing situation

explanation.surface: Someone asks a question they don't want answered in an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting does not expect a reply, and the same phrase, as 'a fine how-d'ye-do', means a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: An old greeting that needs no answer, and also a fuss or awkward predicament.

clue.text: Sticking awkwardly here and there for a start

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters of here and are clumsily rearranged
for a start means only the first letter of the word there

explanation.surface: Something is stuck in an awkward way, here and there, to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherent as an adjective means clinging to something, a synonym of sticking.

clue.text: Hood, boon companion, circumnavigator and plant-hunter

parts.note: the outlaw Robin Hood: his first name stands in here
a boon companion is a jolly friend, an old phrase for a good fellow

explanation.surface: A list of colourful adventurers: an outlaw, a drinking pal, a round-the-world sailor and a botanist.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream, who boasts he can put a girdle round the earth in forty minutes and fetches the magic flower for Oberon.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's mischievous sprite promises to circle the world in forty minutes and is sent to find a love potion's flower.

clue.text: Perhaps led out of turn for contract

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stand outside, with the other piece coming out of their middle
perhaps suggests the word led is only one possible arrangement of its letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: to wind a handle or key is to turn it

explanation.surface: At bridge, a player has perhaps led a card out of turn, spoiling the contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge words 'led', 'turn' and 'contract' all suggest cards, but 'contract' is the verb meaning shrink. 'Perhaps' signals the anagram and 'out of' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to shrink or grow smaller, the verb sense of contract.

clue.text: See about crossbill, second in the stories in Just So

indicators.note: about means one word sits around the others

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, so its diocese is a bishop's see
split as cross plus bill: a cross is X and a bill is an account, AC

indicators.note: second in picks out the second letter of the word stories

explanation.surface: A reader is told to look up the crossbill, the second of Kipling's Just So Stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossbill' looks like a bird but is two pieces: X and AC. 'about' puts X, AC and T (the second letter of 'stories') inside ELY, the see.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'just so' agrees that something is precisely right, the same as saying exactly.

clue.text: Standard measurement for colour-display

parts.note: a standard is a flag carried as an emblem
a pole is an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.surface: A standard unit of measure used for showing colours.
explanation.walkthrough: A pole (also called a rod or perch) is an old British length of 5.5 yards. A ship's or regiment's colours are its flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall staff is where colours, meaning flags, are flown for show.

clue.text: Being swept off one's feet is best!

explanation.surface: Being bowled over by love is the best feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcome means overwhelmed by emotion, and as a verb it means to defeat or best someone.

clue.text: Being bent, fiddled

explanation.surface: Someone bent over, cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowed means curved over, and also played with a bow, as a violinist does on a fiddle.

clue.text: Lock used in attempted US burglary. What a scandal!

definitions.text: attempted US burglary. What a scandal

explanation.surface: A lock used in a botched American break-in caused a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1972 break-in at the Watergate building in Washington led to President Nixon's resignation; the tape left on a door lock exposed the burglars.
explanation.definitionFit: A water gate is a lock gate holding back water, and the 1972 burglary gave its name to the scandal.

clue.text: Bottomless sack to start a hare, say

definitions.text: Bottomless sack to start a hare, say

parts.words: Bottomless sack to start a hare, say
parts.note: a sack without its last letter is a sac, and a soundalike of hare is the thing that grows from it

explanation.definitionFit: A follicle is a small sac in the skin from which a hair grows.

clue.text: Tone down, losing the initial point frequently

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word for tone down

parts.note: to tone something down is to soften it
the first letter of the word is S, which is also a compass point, south

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tone it down, dropping the first point they make.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and frequently are synonyms for something happening many times.

clue.text: New section consisting of reviews

indicators.note: new suggests the word section is given a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A fresh section of the paper is made up of reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are written reviews of a play or book in the press.

clue.text: Break routine in endless course

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
endless means the last letter of the course is cut off

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
a comedian's routine is an act

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break from the routine of an endless course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: An entr'acte is an interval between the acts of a play; 'endless' trims the last letter of the course and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval between acts in a theatre is a pause or break in the show.

clue.text: A royal canine judge

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
a canine is a tooth, and a tooth is a biter

explanation.surface: A judge at a royal dog show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like the dog itself; it is a tooth, or something that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter settles disputes, like a judge or referee.

clue.text: Drill followed by rebel army takes shape

indicators.note: followed by means the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: form is drill, a set routine or exercise

indicators.note: rebel means turn against, so the word for army is turned back to front

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Military drill is followed by a rebel army taking shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebel' is the reversal signal here, and 'takes' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A format is the general layout or shape of something.

clue.text: It's crazy to have left Aunt Dotty in charge

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters of the word aunt are scrambled

explanation.surface: It is mad to leave a dotty old aunt in charge of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like a name for the aunt; it is the anagram signal, turning AUNT into UNAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means mad or wildly foolish, a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: US capital gives no return under a pound? What a yarn!

indicators.note: under means, in a down entry, this piece comes below the one before

parts.note: NY is New York, America's financial capital
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

indicators.note: return means the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: A tall tale about an American city giving nothing back for under a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a story; it is a thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic thread spun into yarn for stockings and fabrics.

clue.text: Stop me returning to pub? Have a try!

indicators.note: returning means the word me is read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A drinker is told not to come back to the pub, then urged to give it a go.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, a stop on trade or publication.

clue.text: Cruise, say, to the islands

annotationWithheld.why: Cruise, say, to the islands (5) for EYOTS: no reading found in which any words give EYOTS (no homophone of a Cruise synonym fits); the scan confirms the wording, so the parse remains unknown

clue.text: Cheerless agricultural work by Gibbon and son

parts.note: cold comfort is consolation that offers no cheer
a farm is the place for agriculture

explanation.surface: A grim farm job done by a man called Gibbon and his son.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibbon plus S (son) gives Gibbons: Stella Gibbons wrote the comic novel of rural gloom; the historian Edward Gibbon is a false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic novel about a gloomy Sussex household is the work in question.

clue.text: This man could accept a token payment

definitions.text: This man could accept a token payment

parts.words: This man could accept a token payment
parts.note: a man's name which, taking in the letter A, becomes the word for money paid as a pledge or deposit

explanation.surface: A man who would settle for a nominal sum.
explanation.walkthrough: Put A inside the name and you get EARNEST, an old word for a token payment that seals a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name which gains the letter A to become the word for a deposit sealing a deal.

clue.text: Certain to change it round in French — being greedy

indicators.note: to change means the letters of the word for certain are rearranged

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: round means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: en is the French for in

explanation.surface: A recipe telling you to stir something round in French, being greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain' must be turned into its synonym before 'to change' shuffles it; 'round' wraps 'it' around the French for in.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for hungry or ravenous, hence greedy.
